title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop: dualityIteratedFlags}
  Let $C \in \mathbb{C}^{s \times m}$ be a matrix of rank $s$ and let
$D \in \mathbb{C}^{m \times \ell}$ be a Gale dual matrix.  The tuple
$(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)$ for $\mathcal{C}_i \subset [m]$ is an iterated circuit of $M(C)$ after removing the singleton elements if and only if the chain
$$E_{\ell - k} \subset \dots \subset E_{\ell} = [m], \quad
E_{i} \coloneqq [m] \setminus \bigcup_{j = 1}^{\ell - i}\mathcal{C}_j$$
is a flag of flats in $M(D)$ with $r_D(E_i) = i$ for all
$i = \ell - k,\dots,\ell$. Moreover,
$$r_C\big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i\big) = s \iff
E_{\ell - k} \text{ is independent in } M(D).$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We know that $E$ is a flat of rank $\ell - 1$ in $M(D)$ (also called a hyperplane) if and only if $[m] \setminus E$ is a circuit in $M(C)$ \cite[Proposition 2.1.6(iii)]{oxley}. By \eqref{eq: contractionRestriction}, $E_{\ell - i}$ is a hyperplane in $M(D)_{\mid E_{\ell -i + 1}}$ (in particular, a flat in $M(D)$ of rank $\ell - i$) for $i = 1,\dots,k$ if and only if $\mathcal{C}_{i} = E_{\ell - i + 1} \setminus E_{\ell - i}$ is a circuit in $M(\bigcup_{j = 1}^{i-1} \mathcal{C}_j)$ for $i = 1,\dots,k$. Therefore, $E_{\ell - k} \subset \dots \subset E_{\ell}$ is a chain of flats in $M(D)$ if and only if $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)$ is an iterated circuit of $M(C)$, up to removing the sets with one element. Using \eqref{rank:dual} the rank of $E_{\ell - k}$ in $M(D)$ equals
    $$r_D(E_{\ell - k}) = \big|E_{\ell - k}\big| + r_C\big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^{k} \mathcal{C}_{i}\big) - s.$$
    Therefore, $E_{\ell - k}$ is independent in $M(D)$ if and only if $r_C\big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^k \mathcal{C}_{i}\big) = s$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X \subseteq [m]$ be a subset with $|X| \ge s+1$, and let $d = \dim \Delta_{X}$. Choose a maximal subset $Y\subseteq X$ such that the set $\{b_i\}_{i \in Y}$ is affinely independent. The number of elements in $Y$ must be $|Y| = d+1$. Since $M$ has rank $s$, any subset of size strictly bigger than $s$ is dependent.

The set $\{b_i\}_{i \in \mathcal{C}}$ corresponding to  $\mathcal{C}$ is affinely independent, implying that $\dim \Delta_{\mathcal{C}} = |\mathcal{C}|-1$, contradicting \eqref{eq:hypotheselemmacircuits}. Therefore $d < s$.

	Since $\varphi([s]) \subseteq \{s+1,\dots,m\}$ is nonempty, we have $|X| \ge s+1$, implying that $\dim \Delta_{X} < s$. Moreover, all the vectors in $L_{\varphi}$ are contained in the linear span of $\Delta_X$ (see \eqref{eq: directionSpaces} later on). Therefore, $\dim L_{\varphi} \le \dim \Delta_{X} < s$.

label: lemma: derivativeCircuit
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: derivativeCircuit}
    Let $V \subset \mathbb{C}^m$ be a vector space of dimension $\ell$ that is not contained in any coordinate hyperplane and let $P: V \xrightarrow[]{} \mathbb{C}$ be a homogeneous polynomial function of degree greater or equal than $m - \ell$. If for all circuit vectors $c$ with $k = |\operatorname{supp}(c)|$, we have that
    $$\partial_c^{k-1}P = 0,$$
    then $P = 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The assertion for a polynomial of degree $d > m - \ell$ can be reduced to the case of a polynomial of degree $m - \ell$ by taking a nonzero partial derivatives of degree $d - m + \ell$.

For the case where $P$ has degree $m - \ell$, the proof follows by induction on $\ell$. If $\ell = 1$, then the only circuit vectors in $V$ have support equal to $[m]$ (as $V$ is not contained in any coordinate hyperplane). If we have a polynomial of degree $m - 1$ whose $(m - 1)$-th derivative equals $0$, then it must be the zero polynomial.

If $\ell > 1$, we may consider the coordinate functions $L_j: V \xrightarrow[]{} \mathbb{C}$ sending a vector $w$ to $w_j$ and the vector spaces $T_j = \ker(L_j)$. Clearly, $T_j \subset V$ is a hyperplane as $V$ is not contained in any coordinate hyperplane. Moreover, any circuit vector in $T_j$ is also a circuit vector in $V$. For each $j \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, consider
$$\mathcal{X}_j = \{j' \in [m] :\: \ker L_{j'} = T_j\}$$
Note that $[m] = \bigsqcup_{j \in \mathcal{X}}\mathcal{X}_{j}$ for some set of representatives $\mathcal{X} \subset [m]$ and let $a_j = |\mathcal{X}_j|$ for $j \in [m]$. In particular, we can always restrict the support of $T_j$ to $\mathbb{C}^{m - a_j}$. For any $v \in V \setminus T_j$ and $0 \leq t \leq a_j - 1$, we may consider the function
$$P_t \coloneqq \partial_v^tP_{\: \mid T_j},$$
which has degree
$m - \ell - t \geq m - a_j - \ell + 1$. Using the hypothesis and that derivatives and restrictions commute, we derive that the functions $P_t$ satisfy the conditions of the lemma. More concretely, for all circuit vectors $c \in T_j$, we have
$$\partial_c^{k - 1}P_t=\partial_c^{k - 1}\partial_v^{t}P_{\mid T_j} = 0.$$
Therefore, $P_t = 0$ in $T_j$ for all $0 \leq t \leq a_j - 1$. As the function $P(w + \lambda v)$ equals
$\sum_{t \geq 0}\frac{\lambda^t}{t!}
(\partial_v^tP)(w)$, the polynomial $L_j^{a_j}$ divides $P$. If we apply this for all $j \in \mathcal{X}$, we deduce that $\prod_{j \in \mathcal{X}} L_j^{a_j}$ (which has degree $m > m - \ell$) divides $P$, implying that $P$ must be the zero polynomial in $V$.

label: prop: contractedCircuit
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: contractedCircuit}
    Let $F = C(u \star x^B)$ be a vertical system. If $F$ is generically consistent, there exists a circuit $\mathcal{C}$ of $M(C)$ with $\dim \Delta_{\mathcal{C}} = r_C(\mathcal{C})$ such that $F_{\mathcal{C}}$ is generically consistent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As $F$ is generically consistent, \Cref{thm:genericConsistencyOSkarElisendaBeatriz} implies that there exists a minor of the matrix $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ which is a nonzero polynomial function on $\ker C \subset \mathbb{C}^m$.

    We denote this minor as $P: \ker(C) \xrightarrow{} \mathbb{C}$ and note that it is a function of degree $s = m - \ell$. Therefore, \Cref{lemma: derivativeCircuit} implies that there exists a circuit vector $c \in \ker C$, i.e. a circuit $\mathcal{C}$ of $M(C)$, such that $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}} = \operatorname{supp}(c)$ and $r = r_C(\mathcal{C}) = |\mathcal{C}| - 1$ and $\partial_c^rP \neq 0$.

    Note that the matrix $C \operatorname{diag}(c)B^{\top}$ can have, at most, rank $r$, as it only involves the columns of $C$ indexed by $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}$. Therefore, using the multilinearity of the chosen minor, the function $P(w + tc)$ has degree at most $r$ in $t$. Since $\partial^r_cP \neq 0$, there exists a vector $w \in \ker(C)$ such that the coefficient of $t^r$ in $P(w+tc)$ is nonzero. Next, we write $C$ in row-reduced echelon form as in \eqref{eq: rref} (in particular, preserving the function $P$ up to constants). This provides a matrix $Q$ for the contracted system $F_{\mathcal{C}}$, which must have rank $s - r$.

    As $c \in \ker C$, the matrix $R \coloneqq C\operatorname{diag}(c)B^{\top}$ has a first block whose rows span $L_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}}$ and then a block of zeros. On the other hand, if we let $Q \coloneqq C_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}}$, the bottom block of $C\operatorname{diag}(w + tc)B^{\top}$ has the form
    $$M = Q\operatorname{diag}(w')\widetilde{B}^{\top},$$
    where $w' = (w_j)_{j \notin \mathcal{C}}$ and $\widetilde{B}$ only preserves the columns of $B$ corresponding to $j \notin \operatorname{\mathcal{C}}$. All in all, the coefficient of $t^r$ in the function $P(w + tc)$ is a minor of the matrix
    \begin{equation}
    \label{eq: RM}
        \begin{pmatrix}
        R \\
        M
    \end{pmatrix}.
    \end{equation}
    As this coefficient is nonzero, the matrix in \eqref{eq: RM} must have rank $s$. In particular, $R$ has rank $r$ implying that $\dim \Delta_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}} = \dim L_{\mathcal{C}} = r$ and the rows in $M$ are linearly independent modulo the rows of $R$, which after projecting to $L_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}}^{\perp}$, implies that
    $$\operatorname{rank}(Q\operatorname{diag}(w')B_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}}^{\top}) = s - r.$$
    By \Cref{thm:genericConsistencyOSkarElisendaBeatriz}, this implies that $F_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}}$ is generically consistent.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label[theorem]{thm:mainTheorem}
	Let $C \in \mathbb{C}^{s \times m}$ be of rank $s$ and let $B \in \mathbb{Z}^{n \times m}$. The following are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The vertically parametrized system $F = C(u \star x^B)$ is generically consistent.
		\item There exists an iterated circuit $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)$ of $M(C)$,  such that
		$$\dim\big(\sum_{j = 1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_j}\big) = s.$$
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To prove that (ii) implies (i), we assume that there exists an iterated circuit $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)$ such that $
		\dim\Big(\sum_{i = 1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}\Big) = s.$
	Let $d_i \coloneqq \dim(\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i})$ for $i = 1,\dots,k$. By \Cref{lemma:simplices}, the set of points $\{b_j\}_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i}$ is affinely independent for $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$. Therefore, we can pick $j_i \in \mathcal{C}_i$ such that
	$$\bigwedge_{i = 1}^k\bigwedge_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i \setminus \{j_i\}}(b_j - b_{j_i}) \neq 0.$$
	We note that $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \cup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i \setminus \{j_1,\dots,j_k\}$ is a basis of $M(C)$  and write $C$ in row-reduced echelon form with respect to $\mathcal{D}$. Let $P \in \mathbb{C}^{s \times \ell}$ be the matrix in \eqref{eq: rref} with respect to the basis $\mathcal{D}$, partitioning $[m]$ into $\mathcal{D} \sqcup ([m] \setminus \mathcal{D})$ . After reordering the columns, we may assume that $\{j_1,\dots,j_k\} = \{s + 1,\dots,s + k\}$, i.e. the first $k$ columns of $P$ correspond to the subset of the remaining elements in the iterated circuit. We denote $D_i = d_1 + \dots + d_i$ for all $i = 1,\dots,k$. As $\mathcal{C}_i$ is a circuit of $M(\mathcal{C}_1 \cup \dots \cup \mathcal{C}_{i-1})$, the support of the $i$-th column is contained in the first $D_i$ rows. In particular, $$P_{j,i} = \begin{cases}
		0 & D_i < j \\
		\neq 0 & D_{i-1} < j \leq D_i
	\end{cases}.$$ Using this, we deduce that the coefficient of the monomial $\prod_{i = 1}^k\lambda_i^{d_i}$ in the polynomial $q(\lambda)$ in \eqref{eq:consistencyPolynomial}
	equals:
	$$\prod_{i = 1}^k\prod_{j = D_{i-1} + 1}^{D_{i}}P_{j,i} \otimes \bigwedge_{i = 1}^k\bigwedge_{j = D_{i-1} + 1}^{D_i}(b_j - b_{s + i}) \neq 0.$$
 Here, we used the convention that $D_0 = 0$. Therefore, by \Cref{lemma_1}, $F = C(u \star x^B)$ is generically consistent.

	For the other implication, we assume that $F$ is generically consistent and proceed by induction on $\ell$. If $\ell = 1$, the polynomial $q(\lambda)$ must be of the form
	$$\Big(\prod_{i = 1}^sP_{i,1} \otimes \bigwedge_{i = 1}^s  \big(b_{s + 1} - b_i \big) \Big)\lambda_1.$$
	Therefore, $q(\lambda)$ is not a zero polynomial if and only if the unique circuit $\mathcal{C}$ in $M(C)$ satisfies $\dim \Delta_{\mathcal{C}} = s$.

    If $\ell > 1$, we use \Cref{prop: contractedCircuit} to deduce that there exists a circuit $\mathcal{C}_1$ such that $F_{\mathcal{C}_1}$ is generically consistent. If $d \coloneqq  r_C(\mathcal{C}_1)$, then the number of rows of $F_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_1}$ is $s - d$, while the number of nonzero columns is, at most, $m - d - 1$. Therefore,
    $$\ell_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_1} = m - d - 1 - (s - d) < \ell.$$
    Applying the induction hypothesis, we deduce that there exists an iterated circuit $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{C}_2,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)$ of $M(\mathcal{C}_1)$ such that
    $$\dim\big(\sum_{j = 2}^k\tau_{\mathcal{C}_1}(\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_j})\big) = s - d$$
    As $\ker \tau_{\mathcal C_1} = L_{\mathcal{C}_1}$, $(\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_1,\dots,\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_k)$ is an iterated circuit of $M(C)$ with $\dim \big(\sum_{j = 1}^k\Delta_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_j}\big) = s$, concluding the proof.

	u_3xy^{-1} + u_5 x^{-1}y = 0.

for $i = \ell - k,\dots,\ell$. Moreover, $E_{\ell - k}$ is independent if and only if $r_C(\cup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i) = s$. If $E_{\ell - k}$ is independent, then the flag can be extended to a complete flag
\begin{equation}
\label{eq: completeFlag}
\emptyset = E_{0} \subset E_1 \subset \dots \subset E_{\ell} = [m], \quad r_D(E_i) = i,
\end{equation}
by considering any flag of independent sets contained in $E_{\ell - k}$.

Next, we consider the vector subspace of $\mathbb{R}^m$:
$$U \coloneqq \{x \in \mathbb{R}^m : \: \operatorname{supp}(x) \subset \bigcup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i, \: \sum_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i}x_j = 0, \: \forall i \in \{1,\dots,k\}\},$$
which has dimension $r_C\big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i\big)$. In addition, consider the linear map defined by the matrix $\overline B$, i.e.
$$\overline{B}: \mathbb{R}^{m} \xrightarrow[]{} \mathbb{R}^{n + 1}, \quad x \xrightarrow[]{} \overline{B} \cdot x.$$
Note that $U$ is the direct sum of the vector spaces
\[
\Big\{(x_j)_{j\in\mathcal C_i}\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal C_i|} \: :
\sum_{j\in\mathcal C_i}x_j=0\Big\}.
\]
The image of each of these vector subspaces under $\overline{B}$ is isomorphic to the real vector spaces $L_{\mathcal{C}_i}$ from \eqref{eq: directionSpaces}, adding a first component equal to zero as the elements in $U$ satisfy that $\sum_{i = 1}^m x_i = 0$. Hence, we deduce that $$\dim \overline{B}(U) = \dim \big(\sum_{i = 1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}\big).$$
Using the rank-nullity theorem, we deduce that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq: rankNullity}
\dim\big(\sum_{i = 1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}\big) = r_C\Big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i\Big) - \dim(U \cap \ker(\overline{B})).
\end{equation}
As the rank of $M(C)$ equals $s$, we have that $\dim(\sum_{i = 1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}) = s$ if and only if $r_C\big(\bigcup_{i = 1}^k\mathcal{C}_i\big) = s$ and $U \cap \ker(\overline{B}) = 0$.

Finally, we note that $x \in \ker(\overline{B})$ if and only if there exists $y \in \mathbb{R}^{m - n - 1}$ such that $x = Gy$, i.e. $x_i = \langle g_i, y\rangle$ for all $i = 1,\dots,m$. Using the complete flag in \eqref{eq: completeFlag}, we let $s_i$ be as in \eqref{eq: si} and note that $x \in U \cap \ker(\overline{B})$ if and only if
$$ \langle s_i,y \rangle = 0, \quad \forall i \in \{1,\dots,\ell\}, $$
for $x = G y$. Therefore, $U \cap \ker(\overline{B}) = 0$ which happens if and only if,
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}} \langle s_j : \; j = 1,\dots,\ell \rangle = \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}} \langle g_j : \: j \in [m] \rangle. $$
Using \Cref{rk: excludesl},  we conclude the proof of (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i). Conversely, by \Cref{prop: dualityIteratedFlags}, a complete flag of flats of $M(D)$ comes from an iterated circuit after omitting the sets $E_i\setminus E_{i-1}$ with one element, which impose $x_j=0$ on $U$ in both cases, and the same computation proves (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii).

label: def: nonsplitting
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def: nonsplitting}
Let $F = C(u \star x^B)$ be a vertical system and let $H = (D(y) \star \frac{1}{u})^{G} - \mathbf{1}$ be its Gale dual system. We say that a flag of flats in $M(D)$
$$\emptyset \subset E_1 \subset \dots \subset E_{k}$$
is \emph{non-splitting} if
$s_i \notin L_{E_{i-1}}^*$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,k-1\}$, where $s_i$ is defined in \eqref{eq: si}.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label[corollary]{cor: nonsplitGspan}
Let $F = C(u \star x^B)$ and let $H = (D(y) \star \frac{1}{u})^{G} - \mathbf{1}$ be its Gale dual. Assume that $s\leq n$. Let $0 \subset E_1 \subset \dots \subset E_\ell = [m]$ be a complete flag of flats in $M(D)$ with $r_D(E_i) = i$ with $i = 1,\dots,\ell - 1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item If the flag is non-splitting, then it is $G$-spanning.
    \item If the flag is $G$-spanning and $
    \dim L_{E_i}^* = i$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,\ell - 1\}$, then it is non-splitting.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $s\leq n$, we have
that the rank of $G$ equals $m-n-1\leq m-s-1=\ell-1$. Suppose first that the flag is non-splitting. Since
$$
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{i-1}\rangle
\subseteq L_{E_{i-1}}^*,
$$
the condition $s_i\notin L_{E_{i-1}}^*$ for
$1\leq i\leq\ell-1$ implies that
$s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$ are linearly independent.
Together with the rank bound and the fact that $\sum_{i = 1}^{\ell} s_i = 0$, this gives
$$
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{\ell}\rangle
=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle g_j:j\in[m]\rangle.
$$
Thus the flag is $G$-spanning.

Conversely, suppose that the flag is $G$-spanning and
$\dim_{\mathbb{R}}L_{E_i}^*=i$ for $1\leq i\leq\ell-1$.
Then
$$
L_{E_{\ell-1}}^*
\subseteq \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle g_j:j\in[m]\rangle
=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}\rangle.
$$
Since the left-hand space has dimension $\ell-1$,
the vectors $s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$ are linearly independent.
For each $1\leq i\leq\ell-1$, we therefore have
$$
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_i\rangle=L_{E_i}^*,
$$
because the left-hand space is contained in the right-hand
space and both have dimension $i$. Consequently,
$$
s_i\notin
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{i-1}\rangle
=L_{E_{i-1}}^*,
\qquad 1\leq i\leq\ell-1.
$$
Hence the flag is non-splitting.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label[corollary]{thm: equivalentConditions}
	Let $F = C(u \star x^B)$ be a vertical system with $\operatorname{rk}(C) = n$. The following are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The tropicalizations of $X_B$ and $Y_{C}$ have a nonempty (stable) intersection.
		\item There exists an iterated circuit $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_{k})$ of $M(C)$ such that $$\dim \big( \sum_{i = 1}^{k} \Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}\big)=n.$$
		\item The mixed volume $\text{MV}(\Delta^{(1)},\Delta^{(2)} - \Delta^{(1)},\dots,\Delta^{(n)} - \Delta^{ (n-1)})$ is positive, where each entry is considered as a multilinear function.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By \cite[Theorem 5.1]{kaveh2025vectorvaluedlaurentpolynomialequations}, \cite[Theorem 3.21]{feliu2026rootboundsverticalsystems} and \Cref{thm:mainTheorem}, the three conditions are equivalent to the system being generically consistent over $\mathbb{T}^n$.

title: Example
body_md:
Consider the system $F = C(u \star x^B)$ with matrices
	$$C = \begin{pmatrix}
		1 & 1 & 1 \\
		0 & 1 & 1
	\end{pmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{pmatrix}
		0 & 1 & 0 \\
		0 & 0 & 1
	\end{pmatrix}.$$
	Note that the only circuit in $M(C)$ consists of the columns $\{2,3\}$. The Newton polytope $$\Delta = \Delta^{(1)} = \textrm{conv} \Big\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\Big\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$$ equals the unit simplex. Moreover, as the second and third columns of $C$ are linearly dependent, $\Delta^{(2)} = \textrm{conv}\Big\{(1,0),(0,1)\Big\}$. Therefore,
	$$\text{MV}(\Delta^{(1)},\Delta^{(2)} - \Delta^{(1)}) = \text{MV}(\Delta^{(1)},\Delta^{(2)}) - \text{MV}(\Delta^{(1)},\Delta^{(1)}) = 1 - 1 = 0.$$
	Equivalently, it can be checked that the system has no iterated circuits $(\mathcal{C}_1, \mathcal{C}_2)$ such that $\dim  \big(\Delta_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_1} +  \Delta_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_2}\big)=2.$ Note that as the first column of $C$ is not contained in any circuit, we have $\operatorname{Trop}(Y_C) = \varnothing$.

title: Proof

We choose $j_i\in\mathcal C_i$ and subsets $K_i\subseteq\mathcal C_i\setminus\{j_i\}$ for each $i = 1,\dots,k$ such that the vectors in $\bigcup_{i = 1}^k\bigcup_{a \in K_i}\{b_a - b_{j_i}\}$ form a basis of the direction space of $\sum_i\Delta_{\mathcal C_i}$, and set $I=\bigcup_i(\mathcal C_i\setminus(K_i\cup\{j_i\}))$.
Since $\bigcup_i(\mathcal C_i\setminus\{j_i\})$ is independent in $M(C)$, the sets $K_i\cup\{j_i\}$ with $K_i\neq\varnothing$ (in their original order) form an iterated circuit of $M(I)$ satisfying \eqref{eq: rIdimDelta}.

label: lemm: sameCircuits
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume (i) holds and consider the linear forms $L_i: \ker(C) \mapsto \mathbb{C}$ to be the projection to the $i$-th coordinate which are nonzero since there are no coloops. If the operators $L_i$ and $L_j$ are not proportional, their kernels would be two different hyperplanes of $\ker(C)$, so some $w \in \ker(C)$ would have $w_j = 0 \neq w_i$. Choose such a $w$ with minimal support. Then, $w$ is a circuit vector: if $w'\in\ker(C)\setminus\{0\}$ has $\operatorname{supp}(w')\subsetneq\operatorname{supp}(w)$, then either $w'_i\neq0$ and $w'$ contradicts the minimality, or $w'_i=0$ and $w-\mu w'$ does, for $\mu$ chosen to cancel one coordinate of $\operatorname{supp}(w')$. Therefore, $\operatorname{supp}(w)$ would be a circuit containing $i$ but not $j$, getting a contradiction.


Conversely, if there exists $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^*$ such that $w_j = \lambda w_i$ then every vector of $\ker(C)$ has either both $i,j$ or neither of them in its support.

label: codimension maximum
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi=(x,u)\in\mathcal W_F$ be a generic point and by generic smoothness, the fibre through $\xi$ is smooth of dimension $n-\operatorname{rank} J_xF(\xi)$. Furthermore, $\dim\mathcal W_F=n+m-s-c$ (where $c$ is the number of connected components of $M(C)$) and hence, by the fiber dimension theorem it suffices to show that $\operatorname{rank} J_xF(\xi)=\iota(F)$. Here, $J_xF(\xi)=C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(x)^{-1}$ with $w=u\star x^B\in\ker(C)$.

As $\mathcal W_F\neq\varnothing$, $M(C)$ has no coloops: if $i$ were a coloop, then $w_i=0$ for every $w\in\ker(C)$, so any $(x,u)\in\mathcal W_F$ would have $u_ix^{b_i}=0$ and hence $u_i=0$, while $\{i\}$ is a connected component and $\mathbb{P}^{\mathcal B_i}=\mathbb{P}^0$ forces $u_i\neq0$. Taking $x=\mathbf 1$, $w$ then ranges over a dense subset of $\ker(C)$. So we must show that the generic rank of $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ on $\ker(C)$ is $\iota(F)$.

Take an iterated circuit attaining $\iota(F)$, and $I$, $Y=\bigcup_i\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_i\setminus I$ as in \Cref{lemma: mC}. After removing linearly dependent rows, the system given by the columns $Y$ of $C$ is generically consistent by \Cref{thm:mainTheorem}. By \Cref{thm:genericConsistencyOSkarElisendaBeatriz}, its matrix $C_I\operatorname{diag}(w')B^{\top}$ has rank $\iota(F)$ for some $w'$ in its kernel. Extending $w'$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$ by adding zeros outside the columns of $C_I$ lift it to some $w\in\ker(C)$. Writing $C$ as in \eqref{equation:contraction}, these rows appear among the rows of $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$. Then $\operatorname{rank} C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top} \geq \iota(F)$.

We show that the rank of $ C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ is less or equal than $\iota(F)$ for all $w\in\ker(C)$ and any $C$, by induction on $m$. The smallest $m$ for which we can have $\mathcal{W}_F \neq \varnothing$ is $m = s + 1$ and we only have $\mathcal{W}_F \neq \varnothing$ when $[m]$ is the unique circuit of $M(C)$. In that case, the rank equals the dimension of the affine span of $\Delta_{[m]}$ i.e. $\iota(F)$. Moreover, we may delete zero columns and coordinates vanishing on $\ker(C)$, and assume $\iota(F)<s$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Suppose two elements of $M(C)$ lie in exactly the same circuits, let $\mathcal A \subset [m]$ be the set of all elements lying in the same circuits as them, and fix $i\in\mathcal A$. By \Cref{lemm: sameCircuits}, there are $v_j\neq0$ with $w_j=v_jw_i$ for all $w\in\ker(C)$ and $j\in\mathcal A$. Let $\widehat F=\widehat C(u\star x^{\widehat B})$, where $\widehat C$ is obtained from $C$ by replacing the columns in $\mathcal A$ by the single column $\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}v_jc_j$, and $\widehat B$ is $B_{\mathcal A}$ with the extra column $\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_i)$. If $\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}v_jc_j = 0$ the new column is a loop of $M(\widehat C)$; deleting this column does not change $\ker(\widehat C)$ or $\iota(\widehat F)$, so we may assume that $\widehat C$ has no zero column. Since $\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_j)=\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_i)$ for $j\in\mathcal A$,
\[
  \sum_{k=1}^m w_k\,c_k\,\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_k)^{\top}=\widehat C\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\widehat B^{\top},\qquad \widehat w=\big((w_k)_{k\notin\mathcal A},w_i\big)\in\ker(\widehat C).
\]
The left-hand side is $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ composed with $\tau_{\mathcal A}^{\top}$. As $\ker\tau_{\mathcal A}=L_{\mathcal A}$, the rank of $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ is at most $\dim\Delta_{\mathcal A}$ plus the rank of this matrix, hence at most $\dim\Delta_{\mathcal A}+\iota(\widehat F)$ by induction. Note that $w\mapsto\widehat w$ is an isomorphism between $\ker(C)$ and $\ker(\widehat C)$, and the relations $w_j=v_jw_i$ for $j\in\mathcal A$ are preserved when we contract by a set not intersecting $\mathcal A$. Since the circuits of a represented matroid are the minimal supports of nonzero kernel vectors and, by \Cref{lemm: sameCircuits}, the support of every $w\in\ker(C)$ contains either all of $\mathcal A$ or none of it, the isomorphism $w\mapsto\widehat w$ carries $\operatorname{supp}(w)$ to the set obtained from it by replacing $\mathcal A$ by the new column, and hence induces a bijection between the circuits of $M(C)$ and those of $M(\widehat C)$. As the relations $w_j=v_jw_i$ persist after contracting by a set disjoint from $\mathcal A$, the same bijection holds for all the successive contractions. Therefore, the iterated circuits of $M(\widehat C)$ are the iterated circuits $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}$ of $M(C)$ where we replace $\mathcal A$ by the new column. As $\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_j)=\tau_{\mathcal A}(b_i)$ for all $j\in\mathcal A$, the corresponding direction spaces of $\widehat F$ are $\tau_{\mathcal A}(L_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_t})$, implying that such an iterated circuit has value
\[
\dim\tau_{\mathcal A}(\Sigma)=\dim(\Sigma+L_{\mathcal A})-\dim\Delta_{\mathcal A}, \quad \text{where } \Sigma\coloneqq\sum_tL_{\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_t}.
\]
If some $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}_i$ in $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}$ contains $\mathcal A$, this is at most $\iota(F)-\dim\Delta_{\mathcal A}$. Otherwise, $\mathcal A$ lies in a further circuit $\mathcal{C}_{k + 1}$ of the contraction with
$$\dim(\Sigma+L_{\mathcal C_{k+1}})\ge\dim(\Sigma+L_{\mathcal A}).$$
Hence, $\iota(\widehat F)\le\iota(F)-\dim\Delta_{\mathcal A}$.

\item Suppose finally that no two elements lie in exactly the same circuits. By \Cref{lemm: sameCircuits}, the $m$ linear forms $L_j$ on $\ker(C)$ are nonzero and pairwise non-proportional for $j \in [m]$. For each $j \in [m]$, the hyperplane $T_j=\{w\in\ker(C):w_j=0\}$ is the kernel of the matrix obtained from $C$ by deleting the column $j \in [m]$, and for $w\in T_j$ the matrix $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$ is the one of the vertical system $F_j$ obtained from $F$ by deleting the column $j$. Every iterated circuit of the matroid of $F_j$ is an iterated circuit of $M(C)$, so $\iota(F_j)\le\iota(F)$. By induction, $\operatorname{rank} C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}\le\iota(F)$ for all $w\in T_j$. Now let $P$ be an $(\iota(F)+1)$-minor of $C\operatorname{diag}(w)B^{\top}$. As in the proof of \Cref{lemma: derivativeCircuit}, $P$ vanishes on every $T_j$. Therefore, the product of the $m$ pairwise non-proportional forms $L_j$ divides $P$. Since $\deg P=\iota(F)+1\le s<m$, we get $P=0$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label[corollary]{prop: codimFlags}
Let $F=C(u\star x^B)$ be a vertical system with $ \operatorname{rk}(C)=s$ and $\mathcal W_F\neq\varnothing$. For a complete flag $\varnothing=E_0\subset E_1\subset\dots\subset E_\ell=[m]$ of flats of $M(D)$ with $r_D(E_i)=i$, let $s_1,\dots,s_\ell$ be as in \eqref{eq: si}. Then
\[
\operatorname{codim}\big(\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}\big)=(m-n-1)-\max\,\dim\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}\rangle,
\]
where the maximum is taken over all such complete flags.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{thm:mainCodimension}, the codimension equals $s-\iota(F)$. Since $\mathcal W_F\neq\varnothing$, $M(C)$ has no coloops, so an iterated circuit whose union has rank smaller than $s$ can be extended by a circuit of the contraction with at least two elements. This does not decrease the dimension of the Minkowski sum, so $\iota(F)$ is attained by an iterated circuit whose union has rank $s$. For such an iterated circuit and the complete flag \eqref{eq: completeFlag}, the proof of \Cref{thm: GspanningFlag} shows that $\dim\big(\sum_i\Delta_{\mathcal C_i}\big)=s-\dim(U\cap\ker\overline B)$ and that $U\cap\ker\overline B$ is isomorphic to $\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{m-n-1}:\langle s_i,y\rangle=0\text{ for all }i\}$. Hence
\[
\dim\Big(\sum_i\Delta_{\mathcal C_i}\Big)=s-(m-n-1)+\dim\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{\ell}\rangle.
\]
Conversely, as in the proof of \Cref{thm: GspanningFlag}, every complete flag arises in this way from an iterated circuit whose union has rank $s$, after omitting the sets $E_i\setminus E_{i-1}$ with one element. Finally, $\sum_is_i=\sum_jg_j=0$, so $s_\ell$ lies in the span of $s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$. Taking the maximum over all complete flags proves the claim.

label: thm: dualDefects
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: dualDefects}
        Let $B \in \mathbb{Z}^{n \times m}$ be a matrix and $F$ be the vertical system in \eqref{eq: FB}. The following are equivalent:
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
            \item $X_B$ is defective.
            \item For all iterated circuits  $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_{k})$ in $M(\overline{B})$, we have
            $$\dim\big(\sum_{i = 1}^{k} \Delta_{\mathcal{C}_i}\big) < n.$$
            \item All non-splitting flags in $M(G)$ have length $< \ell$.
            \item For every complete flag of flats in $M(G)$, the vectors $s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$ in \eqref{eq: si} are linearly dependent.
        \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The equivalence between (i) and (ii) follows from \Cref{thm:mainCodimension}. Here, $C=\overline{B}$, so $s=n+1$ and $\ell=m-n-1$, and we may take $D=G$. In particular, $M(D)=M(G)$ and $\dim L_E^*=r_G(E)$ for every $E\subseteq[m]$. If $\mathcal W_F=\varnothing$, then $M(G)$ has loops, so there are no complete flags with $E_0=\varnothing$, and (i), (iii) and (iv) hold. Otherwise, by \Cref{prop: codimFlags}, the codimension of $\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ equals $\ell-\max\dim\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\langle s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}\rangle$. So it is larger than one if and only if $s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$ are linearly dependent for every complete flag, proving that (i) and (iv) are equivalent. Finally, a flag of length $\ell$ is complete, and since $\dim L_{E_i}^*=i$, the arguments in the proof of \Cref{cor: nonsplitGspan} show that a complete flag is non-splitting if and only if $s_1,\dots,s_{\ell-1}$ are linearly independent. This proves the equivalence between (iii) and (iv).

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label[theorem]{thm: codimensionOne}
	Let $F = C(u \star x^B)$ be a vertical system and assume that $F$ is not generically consistent and $\mathcal{W}_F \neq \varnothing$. The projection $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_{F})}$ has codimension $1$ if and only if there exists $i \in [m]$ such that the system $F_{(i)} = C_{(i)}(u \star x^B)$ is generically consistent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ has codimension $1$. By \Cref{thm:mainCodimension}, we have
$\iota(F)=s-1$. Choose an iterated circuit
$\mathcal C=(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_k)$
such that
$\dim\left(\sum_{j=1}^k\Delta_{\mathcal C_j}\right)=s-1.$ Since $\mathcal W_F\neq\varnothing$, $M(C)$ has no coloops, so we may extend $\mathcal C$ until $r_C(\bigcup_j\mathcal C_j)=s$, and the dimension of the Minkowski sum remains $s-1$.

Choose $j_t\in\mathcal C_t$ and $K_t\subseteq\mathcal C_t\setminus\{j_t\}$ as in the proof of \Cref{lemma: mC}, so that $\sum_t|K_t|=s-1$. Then $\mathcal D=\bigcup_t(\mathcal C_t\setminus\{j_t\})$ is a basis of $M(C)$ with exactly one element $i\notin\bigcup_tK_t$, say $i\in\mathcal C_{t_0}$. As $\mathcal D$ is independent, contracting $i$ does not change $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_{t_0-1}$, and $\mathcal C_{t_0}\setminus\{i\}$ is a circuit of $M(\mathcal C_1\cup\dots\cup\mathcal C_{t_0-1}\cup\{i\})$. Omitting it if it has one element, we obtain an iterated circuit of $M(\{i\})$ whose Minkowski sum contains the vectors $b_a-b_{j_t}$, $a\in K_t$, and hence has dimension $s-1$. By \Cref{thm:mainTheorem}, $F_{(i)}$ is generically consistent.

Conversely, suppose that $F_{(i)}$ is generically consistent for some
$i\in[m]$. The system $F$ is obtained from $F_{(i)}$ by imposing one
additional equation, which is the only one containing $u_i$ when $C$ is written in row-reduced echelon form with respect to a basis containing $i$. So, for generic $(u_j)_{j\neq i}$ and a zero $x$ of $F_{(i)}$, this equation can be solved for $u_i$. Hence $\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ has codimension at most 1. Since $F$ is not generically consistent,
$\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ is a proper subvariety of the parameter
space, and therefore has positive codimension. It follows that
$\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ has codimension $1$.

\label[definition]{def: resultant}

We call a \emph{resultant} $\operatorname{Res}_F$ of the vertical system $F$ to be any irreducible polynomial in $\mathbb{C}[u]$ that vanishes over $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_F)}$ in $\mathbb{P}^{\mathcal{B}}$.

title: Corollary

title: Proof
body_md:
We denote by $\mathcal{W}_i$ the incidence variety of $F_{(i)}$. If the system $F_{(i)}$ is generically inconsistent, then $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_i)}$is not the whole parameter space. As a consequence,
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item There exists an irreducible polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[u_j : \: j \neq i]$ that vanishes in $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_{i})}$, and hence on $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_F)}$, since the equations of $F_{(i)}$ are among those of $F$ after row reduction with respect to the column $i$.
		\item As $\operatorname{Res}_F$ is irreducible, we have that the variable $u_i$ does not divide $\operatorname{Res}_F$.
	\end{enumerate}
	In particular, if $\operatorname{Res}_F \notin \mathbb{C}[u_j : \: j \neq i]$, then $\operatorname{Res}_F$ is a nonzero divisor in $\mathbb{C}[u]/\langle p\rangle$. As both $\operatorname{Res}_F$ and $p$ vanish on $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_{F})}$, $\operatorname{codim} (\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_{F})}) \geq 2$, leading to a contradiction. Conversely, if $\operatorname{Res}_F \in \mathbb{C}[u_j : \: j \neq i]$, then $\overline{\pi(\mathcal{W}_{i})}$ is not the whole parameter space: otherwise, as in the proof of \Cref{thm: codimensionOne}, for generic $(u_j)_{j\neq i}$ there is $u_i$ leading to $u\in\pi(\mathcal W_F)$, and $\operatorname{Res}_F$ would vanish identically. This implies that the system $F_{(i)}$ is not generically consistent.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop: sparseResultant}
Let $F=C(u\star x^B)$ be a vertical system with
$C\in\mathbb C^{(n+1)\times m}$ of rank $n+1$, and assume that
$\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_F)}$ has codimension one. If $P_B\bigl(\det(C_I)u_I\bigr)\neq0$ and $\deg(\operatorname{Res}_B)=\deg(\operatorname{Res}_F)$, then
\[
\operatorname{Res}_F=P_B\bigl(\det(C_I)u_I\bigr),
\]
up to a nonzero scalar, where $C_I$ denotes the submatrix of $C$ with columns indexed by $I \subset [m]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $u\in\mathbb C^m$ satisfy $\operatorname{Res}_F(u)=0$. Then $F_u$ has a solution
in $\mathbb T^n$. Consider the specialization
\[
\bar u_{i,j}\coloneqq c_{i,j}u_j.
\]
The resulting sparse system is precisely $F_u$, and hence
\[
\operatorname{Res}_B\bigl((c_{i,j}u_j)_{i,j}\bigr)=0.
\]
For $I=\{j_0,\ldots,j_n\}$, we have
\[
[j_0\cdots j_n]
=
\det
\begin{pmatrix}
c_{0,j_0}u_{j_0} & \cdots & c_{0,j_n}u_{j_n}\\
\vdots & & \vdots\\
c_{n,j_0}u_{j_0} & \cdots & c_{n,j_n}u_{j_n}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\det(C_I)u_I.
\]
Thus $\operatorname{Res}_F$ divides $P_B(\det(C_I)u_I)$. Since these two polynomials
have the same degree, they are equal up to a nonzero scalar.

title: Proof
body_md:
We treat the two cases separately.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Since $\ell=1$, the Gale-dual system consists of the binomial
equation
\[
\prod_{g_j>0}
\left(\frac{d_j}{u_j}\right)^{g_j}
-
\prod_{g_j<0}
\left(\frac{d_j}{u_j}\right)^{-g_j}
=0.
\]
After clearing denominators, this is the polynomial in
\eqref{eq: ResFl1}. The entries of $G$ have greatest common divisor one,
so this binomial is irreducible. Its zero set is the resultant
hypersurface, proving the claim.
\item Without loss of generality, we assume that $d_{2j}$ $\neq 0$ for all $j\in[m]$ and let $
y_j=-\frac{d_{1j}}{d_{2j}}$. The common zero set of $h_1$ and $h_2$ in
\[
\mathbb C\setminus\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}
\]
is the zero set of the Gale-dual system. Hence, by Gale duality, its
projection to the parameter space is the resultant hypersurface
$V(\operatorname{Res}_F)$.

We claim that no boundary point $y_i$ contributes a hypersurface factor
to $\operatorname{Res}_y(h_1,h_2)$. Since no two columns of $D$ are proportional,
\[
d_{1j}+d_{2j}y_i\neq0
\qquad\text{for every }j\neq i.
\]
If $g_{ia}\neq0$ for some $a\in\{1,2\}$, then exactly one of the two
monomials defining $h_a(y_i)$ vanishes, whereas the other is nonzero.
Thus, $h_a(y_i)\neq0$. If $g_i=0$, then $h_1(y_i)$ and $h_2(y_i)$ are Laurent binomials in $u$
whose exponent differences are the two independent columns of $G$.
Their common zero locus has codimension two. Therefore the boundary
points $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ do not contribute a codimension-one component
to the Sylvester resultant. The zero locus of $\operatorname{Res}_y(h_1,h_2)$ in $(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$ consequently has the unique
codimension-one component $V(\operatorname{Res}_F)$. Since $\operatorname{Res}_F$ is irreducible,
there exists $e\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ such that
\[
\operatorname{Res}_y(h_1,h_2)=\operatorname{Res}_F^e
\]
up to multiplication by a nonzero scalar and a monomial in $u$. \qedhere
\end{enumerate}

title: Definition
body_md:
\label[definition]{def: linearlyDegenerate}
	A vertically parametrized polynomial system $F = C(u \star x^B)$ is \emph{linearly degenerate} with respect to $x_i$ if there exist $a_1,\dots,a_k \in \mathbb{C}^*$ such that $V_{\mathbb{T}^n}(F_{u}) \subset \bigcup_{j = 1}^k \{x_i = a_j\}$ for generic values of $u \in \mathbb{C}^m$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label[theorem]{thm: linearDegeneracy}
Let \(F=C(u\star x^B)\) be a generically consistent vertical system with
\(\operatorname{rank}(C)=s\). The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item The vertically parametrized family \(F\) is linearly
    degenerate with respect to \(x_i\).

    \item For every iterated circuit
    \((\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)\) of \(M(C)\),
    \[
    \dim\left(
        \sum_{j=1}^k\tau_i(\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_j})
    \right)<s.
    \]

    \item The polynomial \(R_i\) is nonzero and $\langle F\rangle\cap\mathbb{C}(u)[x_i^{\pm}]=\langle R_i\rangle$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Theorem~4.4]{feliu2025genericgeometrysteadystate}, the family
\(F\) is linearly degenerate with respect to \(x_i\) if and only if
\(\widehat{F}_i\) is generically inconsistent. By
\Cref{thm:mainTheorem}, this is equivalent to
\[
\dim\left(
    \sum_{j=1}^k\tau_i(\Delta_{\mathcal{C}_j})
\right)<s
\]
for every iterated circuit
\((\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_k)\) of \(M(C)\). This proves the
equivalence of (i) and (ii). Moreover, \cite[Theorem~4.4]{feliu2025genericgeometrysteadystate}
shows that these conditions are equivalent to the elimination ideal
\(\langle F\rangle\cap\mathbb{C}(u)[x_i^{\pm}]\) being generated by one nonconstant polynomial $g$. If (iii) holds, then $R_i$ is such a generator, as $\langle F\rangle\neq(1)$ since $F$ is generically consistent. Conversely, assume (i). For $x\in\mathbb{T}^n$, let $x'$ be $x$ without its $i$-th coordinate and $\overline u=(u_jx_i^{b_{ij}})_j$, so that $C(u\star x^B)=C(\overline u\star x'^{B_i})$. The map $(u,x_i)\mapsto\overline u$ has one-dimensional fibres, $V_{\mathbb{T}^n}(F_u)$ is nonempty for generic $u$, and $\widehat F_i$ is not generically consistent. Hence $\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_i)}$ has codimension one, and $R_i$ is well-defined. For generic $u$, the zeros of $R_i(\cdot,u)$ are exactly the values of $x_i$ on $V_{\mathbb{T}^n}(F_u)$, since the points of $\overline{\pi(\mathcal W_i)}$ outside $\pi(\mathcal W_i)$ form a subset of codimension at least two. Moreover, $R_i$ is squarefree, being the pullback of the irreducible polynomial $\operatorname{Res}_{\widehat F_i}$ under the smooth map $(u,x_i)\mapsto\overline u$, and $g$ is squarefree, since for generic $u$ the zeros of $F_u$ are nondegenerate \cite[Theorem~3.7]{FELIU2025630}, so that $\langle F\rangle$ is radical. Hence $R_i$ and $g$ agree up to a unit. This proves the equivalence with (iii).
